title: Palair Macedonian Airlines 301
summary: The Fokker 100 crashed shortly after takeoff in snowy conditions due to ice accumulation on the wings. The aircraft had been parked in snow and refueled; ice around the wing roots melted from fuel temperature but ice on the wingtips remained. The crew elected not to de-ice the aircraft and encountered control problems during takeoff that caused the crash.

The aircraft eventually encountered control problems during takeoff, which caused it to crash.

title: China Eastern Airlines 583
summary: China Eastern Airlines Flight 583 experienced a severe in-flight upset during cruise near the Aleutian Islands at 296 knots when a relief crew member accidentally deployed the leading-edge slats while attempting to fix a speed indicator issue. The unintended slat deployment caused the aircraft nose to pitch up. The pilot then over-corrected the elevator, causing severe oscillations that resulted in a loss of about 5,000 feet of altitude. The aircraft eventually stabilized and made an emergency landing at Shemya Air Force Base.

title: Japan Air System 451
summary: Japan Air System Flight 451, a Douglas DC-9-41 with 72 passengers and 5 crew, was landing at Hanamaki Airport on 18 April 1993 after a short flight from Nagoya when it encountered windshear on final approach. Wind suddenly changed from 240° to 320° gusting 26 to 47 knots at 300 feet altitude. The relatively inexperienced first officer, who was at the controls, failed to recognize the condition and initiate a go-around. The aircraft made a hard landing with such force that the landing gear root penetrated the wing and punctured the fuel tank, causing a fire. All 77 occupants survived and evacuated quickly, with 19 sustaining injuries.

All 25 passengers and five crew members were killed. The aircraft had previously experienced engine problems in Brazzaville but continued to Libreville where the left engine caught fire and failed. The pilot, who had also flown the team from Mauritius the previous day, mistakenly shut down the right engine in response, causing the aircraft to lose all power during climb and fall into the water 500 meters offshore.

Contributing factors included the company's failure to adequately address the captain's previously identified deficiencies and inadequate surveillance and oversight by the FAA.

title: Kuban Airlines 5719
summary: Flight 5719 departed Krasnodar for Gyumri. During approach, the crew boarded 31 passengers in violation of the manifest which listed 6 passengers, causing the aircraft to exceed its maximum takeoff weight of 2,246 kg. The aircraft stalled during a go-around attempt on approach and crashed, killing 35 of 36 occupants.
